paragraphs.title: The Vision of the Lord and the Seraphim

answers: Upon a throne in the temple
easy.explanation: Isaiah saw the Lord sitting upon a high and lifted-up throne, and His train filled the temple.
easy.q: Where did Isaiah see the Lord?

easy.explanation: The KJV says that each seraphim had six wings.
easy.q: How many wings did each seraphim have?

easy.explanation: They cried, “Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts.”
easy.q: What did the seraphim cry to one another?

answers: They covered their faces and feet and flew with two wings
medium.explanation: Each seraphim covered his face with two wings, his feet with two, and flew with two.
medium.q: What did the seraphim do with their wings?

answers: The doorposts moved and the house filled with smoke
medium.explanation: The voice caused the posts of the door to move, and the house was filled with smoke.
medium.q: What happened when the seraph cried?

medium.explanation: The posts are the structural supports of the temple doorway that moved at the voice.
medium.q: What are the “posts of the door” in this passage?

answers: The Lord’s glory fills the whole earth
challenge.explanation: The seraphim declare that the Lord’s glory is present throughout the whole earth.
challenge.q: What does the statement “the whole earth is full of his glory” teach?

answers: Smoke, throne, seraphim, and then the cry
Throne, seraphim, the cry, and then moving doorposts and smoke
The cry, throne, smoke, and then seraphim
challenge.explanation: Isaiah first saw the throne and seraphim; their cry was followed by the moving doorposts and smoke.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Isaiah’s vision?

answers: They showed reverence before the Lord
They were hiding from the smoke
challenge.explanation: Their actions express humility and reverence in the presence of the holy Lord.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the seraphim covering their faces and feet?

paragraphs.title: The Prophet’s Impure Lips and Purification

easy.explanation: Isaiah said, “I am a man of unclean lips.”

answers: A live coal from the altar
easy.explanation: The seraphim carried a live coal taken with tongs from the altar.
easy.q: What did one of the seraphim carry to Isaiah?

easy.explanation: The seraphim laid the coal upon Isaiah’s mouth and said that it had touched his lips.
easy.q: Where did the seraphim place the coal?

answers: He recognized the uncleanness of his lips
He could not see the seraphim
medium.explanation: Isaiah became aware of his own uncleanness when he saw the King, the Lord of hosts.
medium.q: Why did Isaiah feel unworthy after seeing the Lord?

medium.explanation: Isaiah felt ruined and overwhelmed because he had seen the holy King while recognizing his own uncleanness.
medium.q: What does “I am undone” mean in this passage?

answers: His iniquity was taken away and his sin purged
He had to leave the temple
medium.explanation: The seraphim declared, “thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.”
medium.q: What did the seraphim tell Isaiah after touching his lips?

answers: The seraphim purified the part Isaiah had identified as unclean
The seraphim punished Isaiah for seeing the Lord
challenge.explanation: Isaiah confessed that his lips were unclean, and the seraphim touched his lips with the live coal.
challenge.q: What is the connection between Isaiah’s unclean lips and the seraphim’s action?

answers: He went from being unclean and overwhelmed to having his iniquity taken away
He changed from a prophet into a seraphim
He changed from seeing smoke to becoming a king
challenge.explanation: At first Isaiah felt ruined because of his uncleanness; afterward, his sin was purged.
challenge.q: How did Isaiah’s condition change between verses 5 and 7?

challenge.explanation: The KJV says the seraphim took the live coal with tongs from off the altar.
challenge.q: Where did the seraphim get the live coal?

paragraphs.title: The Prophet’s Mission and the People’s Unresponsiveness

answers: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?
easy.explanation: The Lord asked, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?”
easy.q: What did the voice of the Lord ask?

easy.explanation: Isaiah willingly answered, “Here am I; send me.”

answers: They would hear without understanding and see without perceiving
They would neither hear nor see
easy.explanation: Isaiah was told to say, “Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.”
easy.q: What would the people do according to the message?

answers: To deliver a prophetic message and warning
To give instructions for building the temple
To announce the appointment of a king
medium.explanation: Isaiah was sent to speak the Lord’s prophetic message to the people.
medium.q: What was Isaiah’s mission to the people?

answers: Make their hearts unresponsive to understanding
medium.explanation: The surrounding words describe people who do not understand, perceive, or turn to be healed.
medium.q: What does “Make the heart of this people fat” mean in context?

answers: The people hear but do not understand
The people do not hear at all
medium.explanation: The people are told to hear but not understand the message.
medium.q: What relationship between hearing and understanding is described?

answers: He is now ready to accept the mission
He wants to become a king
He wants to leave the temple
challenge.explanation: After his sin was purged, Isaiah responded willingly to the Lord’s call.
challenge.q: Why is Isaiah’s answer, “Here am I; send me,” significant after his purification?

answers: He must speak to people who hear but do not understand
He must speak without receiving a commission
He must hide the prophetic message
challenge.explanation: Isaiah is sent to proclaim the message even though the people will not properly understand or perceive it.
challenge.q: What is the central tension in Isaiah’s mission?

answers: The people’s failure to receive the prophetic message
The appearance of the temple alone
A command for the people only to close their eyes
challenge.explanation: The repeated terms show that the people possess senses but remain spiritually unresponsive.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated references to hearing, seeing, and understanding?

paragraphs.title: Desolation and the Survival of the Holy Seed

answers: Until the people built new houses
Until the cities and houses were empty and the land was desolate
easy.explanation: The answer describes wasted cities, houses without people, and land that is utterly desolate.
easy.q: How long would Isaiah’s mission continue?

answers: The Lord would remove them far away
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord would have removed men far away.
easy.q: What would happen to the people?

easy.explanation: The passage ends by saying, “so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.”
easy.q: What would remain in the end?

answers: Desolation, removal of people, and the survival of a tenth and a holy seed
A holy seed, rebuilt cities, and then desolation
Removal of people, new houses, and prosperity
medium.explanation: The prophecy moves from desolation and removal to the survival of a tenth and the holy seed.
medium.q: What sequence is described in the prophecy?

answers: One-tenth of the people or remnant
medium.explanation: A tenth refers to a surviving portion or remnant left after the devastation.
medium.q: What does “a tenth” mean in this passage?

answers: It would be tested or consumed by fire
It would immediately leave the land
medium.explanation: The passage says, “it shall return, and shall be eaten,” describing a further refining or consuming process.
medium.q: What would happen to the tenth that remained?

answers: A surviving foundation or seed after the tree is cut down
challenge.explanation: Though the trees cast their leaves, their substance remains, illustrating the surviving holy seed.
challenge.q: What do the terebinth and oak represent at the end of the passage?

answers: A tenth remains after the devastation, and a holy seed survives
The people immediately return to the cities
challenge.explanation: The passage describes severe judgment but also preserves a remnant and a holy seed.
challenge.q: How do desolation and hope exist together in these verses?

answers: Something remains even after the tree casts its leaves
The trees were removed without leaving anything
The trees covered the whole earth
challenge.explanation: The trees retain their substance after losing their leaves, just as the holy seed remains after judgment.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the comparison with the terebinth and oak?
